summary: Visible change: the stop notice after a limit now says what was done and what is open, and the chat shows a Continue button (German Weitermachen) that continues the stopped turn with a fresh budget and never retries a write call attempted before the stop.
howTo: Nothing to do with createAiChatHandler and useVercelAiChatTransport. Own budgetStopTexts or locales can set the new keys done, open, openUnanswered ({items}), continueHint (points to the button below) and continueTypedHint (only after the 3rd continuation); a UI without the button sets its own continueHint. The click sends glirastesContinuation: 'budget' in the chat request body: a backend that validates the body strictly must allow that field. The repeat guard covers the continuation and the approval and UI outcome requests after it; a typed follow-up is a new turn without it. Each continuation gets a fresh per-request budget, so time and cost of one question can reach 4x the limits; a managed policy has no switch for continuations yet. onFinish reports continuation: 'budget'; metrics report it as a normal turn.finished. A custom ChatTransport adds continueAfterBudgetStop() (resend the history with that body field) or the button is not shown; a custom MessageParts layout that drops children places the new continuation node. The German continueButton text is now Weitermachen (also on the truncation banner). A customStreamHandler gets no continuation (400). See docs/managed-runtime-sync.md, Continuing a stopped turn.
